publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Artificial Wisdom is advancement of Artificial Intelligence where wisdom should be recognized with the intelligence. It means the constructive behavior and values of humanity need to be the part of Artificial intelligence by incorporating wisdom. These can be demonstrates by simulating thought process and hence thinking ability of human beings is recognized as the consciousness. Currently researchers are working on thoughts and consciousness. These thoughts are coexisted with the particular mental factor. Abhidhamma model of ancient Indian literature are claimed 52 mental factors which are categorized in basic three classes such as Ethically Variable Factor, Unwholesome Factor and Beautiful Factor. Proposed model demonstrates the classification of the mental states. Dataset consists of 445 samples collected from various respondents by asking three questions. Preprocessing is performed by using the techniques of Natural language processing and Non-axiomatic logic. Convolutional Neural Network Machine learning technique applied to classify the mental factors. Performance of the proposed system is measured by applying statistical measures such as Accuracy, Precision, Specificity, Recall and F1-Score. Accuracy for small and large database is obtained as 86.92 percent and 93.02 percent respectively.

articleTitle: Novel Dual Powered Induction Cooktop
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The paper proposes a novel method of induction heating through both ac and dc supply. The ac supply is from the utility mains and the dc supply is from the solar PV. A single stage conversion employed to convert the ac and dc source into a pre-set dc value. The resulting dc is converted into pulsating dc to obtain the desired effect on the work coil to produce heating via induction. The work coil gets energized and induces eddy currents onto the subject (ferromagnetic material), thus leading to the heating up of the subject. The conversion of low voltage, medium power ac and dc supply to medium voltage, medium power is effected through two different control schemes: ac-dc control scheme employs reference current generation technique and pulses are produced using variable frequency hysteresis controller; dc-dc control scheme produces pulses using fixed frequency controller. The work coil is seen heated up as in the conventional case and the heating of work coil with both ac and dc supply with single power conversion claims the merit of the work. The entire work has been validated as Software-in-Loop (SiL) using a real time dSPACE DS1104 Controller.

articleTitle: Close-Grained Classification of Military Aircrafts
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Aircraft recognition is a visual skill and crucial for air defence and military surveillance. It is used for intelligence gathering. Recognition techniques generally depend on external appearance, silhouette, and size. Now a days aircraft design has adapted a wide range of structural variations. Automatic recognition from aerial views is not only challenging but may involve a heavy payoff for erogenous results. The major contribution of this work is to evaluate the transfer learning pipeline with SVM and MLP as the final classifier for aircraft recognition. Additionally, the work proposes a novel framework of closed-grained scenarios. A visual image of an aircraft is possible from the ground with the sky as the background or from the air with earth as the background. We call these as flying and resting crafts respectively. Experimentation for resting crafts is carried out on the existing benchmark MTARSI dataset. A dataset consisting of only flying military aircraft is an ancillary contribution to this work. Conventional CNN results are elated by using the state-of-art feature extraction approach followed by the stacking of SVM and MLP classification models. The proposed closed-grained approach is constrained to the stipulation that visualized image is an aircraft and the goal is to identify the category. Closed grain analysis ensures no confusion due to aircraft-like structural isometric objects which never be noticed flying. Results in the form of a confusion matrix, for various combinations of datasets and models, are shown and analysed. A modified hinge loss function is considered to address limitless error possibility, which outperformed the previously mentioned combinations.

articleTitle: Design and Performance analysis of Net Metering-based Grid Connected Solar Photo-Voltaic System
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Solar energy is the considered to be the most promising source of energy of near future. There is a concern about the utilization of solar energy in Indian subcontinent due to its variable nature and high initial cost. It would be unrealistic to say that the solar energy will replace the conventional thermal energy resources in future but can surely complement them to meet energy demands. Solar photovoltaic energy resources lag the utilization due to its reduced reliability and high initial cost. Hence, it is highly preferred to operate the solar PV systems on net metering basis. The paper attempts to design and analyse the performance of 5.4 KWp grid tied solar PV system on net metering basis for the location of Nagpur, Maharashtra, India (Lat:21.1458° N, long:79.0882° E) specifically discussing Temperature-Irradiance characteristics, Energy flow graph, Energy production forecast with consumption, optimized cost economics of net metering system. The paper also discusses all the electrical and geographical parameters associated with grid tied PV system and analyses the performance of the system. The software used for the design, optimization and analysis is PVSOL2021.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Segmentation using LinkNet
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The brain tumor is a common, yet very deadly disease generally found in adults. The brain tumor is the growth of abnormal cells in the brain, which may lead to cancer. The clinical routine involves a diagnosis of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images manually which is difficult, time-consuming and is prone to human errors. Semantic segmentation is commonly used in medical imaging to identify the precise location and shape of structures in the body and is essential to the proper assessment of medical disorders and their treatment. The proposed model draws on recent success of deep learning methods for semantic segmentation. This paper aims to compare the performance of various transfer learning models such as Inception, ResNet, and ResNext when embedded with the LinkNet architecture. The performance of these models was measured on a dataset consisting of around 4000 MRI scan image pairs. The Dice Coefficient in percentage is 94%.

articleTitle: Autonomous Scheduling and Routing System to Maximize Machine Shop Throughput
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Scheduling and Routing are very crucial variables which affect the throughput of the system. Scheduling and Routing decide ‘When’ and ‘Where’ the activity will be done. Researched system is collective use of computational techniques with machine data integration for optimum scheduling and routing of material on shop floor. This is done by amalgamating traditional techniques and methodologies with modern computational solutions. This autonomous system deployed in and for the industry is hard wired using ESP32 and Raspberry Pi 4 (8GB). This system monitors and reports using the microcontroller circuit based on inputs of machines and stores it. This data is then used to analyze the shop floor and take required decisions. This system is designed to integrate 3 CNC lathe machines, 2 Vertical Machining Center machines and a Horizontal Machining Center for continuous computing and reporting of the machines. The idea is quite simple; the data from the machines is mapped on to a standard data frame defined in Raspberry Pi through ESP32 and finally computed as per the algorithm defined. Raspberry Pi is given capability to display the results real time on its display protocol or share them over its serial or wireless interfaces. The system performance is highlighted by the approximate 9.5% actual time saving in contrast to the theoretical master schedule which suggested 12.643% over the traditional schedule of the company.

articleTitle: Salient Feature of State Observer in FCS-MPC for an Uninterruptible Power Supply
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: A prediction model, a cost function and an optimization algorithm grouped together to form a Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC). As a result, the FCS-success MPC's is dependent on the proper design of these three aspects. The impact of prediction model for an uninterruptible power supply is examined in this paper. Unpredictability of the load connected to VSI makes challenging condition for prediction model design. Rather than using traditional prediction approaches, a Kalman filter (KF) is utilised as a state observer to improve the MPC. The Kalman filter is very resistant to system parameter changes and noise. Comparative study of FCS-MPC of three phase VSI with and without state observer is carried out in this article. Simulation results shows a better result when state observer is used.

articleTitle: A Survey on Authentication Schemes in Multiserver Environment
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Authentication is a mandatory factor in network security since decades. Conventional authentication schemes failed to improve system's security, performance and scalability thus, two-factor, three factor and multifactor authentication schemes are developed. As technology grows, from single server authentication to multiserver authentication schemes and protocols are emerged. Single to multifactor authentication can be used as per the aspect and field of study. Different aspects may use different cryptographic schemes, key agreement to improve security, performance and scalability.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of OFDM and OQAM/FBMC based Communication Networks under Vehicular Channel Models: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: In this paper, performance analysis of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) as well as offset quadrature amplitude modulation (OQAM)/ filter bank multicarrier (FBMC) based communication network is carried out under the influence of vehicular channels. The vehicular channel models such as vehicular A and vehicular B are considered for this investigation. Further, the effect of prototype filter PHYDYAS on performance of the above mentioned networks is examined. Zero forcing (ZF) equalizer is deployed at the receiver for signal reconstruction. It is observed that OQAM/FBMC outperforms OFDM in high mobility condition whereas under low mobility conditions, their performances are almost identical.

articleTitle: Risk Management and Safety Assessment in Building Construction Projects
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Construction workers fatality rate is more when compared with workers of any other sectors. To minimize the number of risks and maximize the safety, construction companies seeks different strategies constantly. This study focuses on the issues and uncertainties in various activities of construction projects in the state of Kerala. The most important key factor in safety management system is the increasing accident rate in construction sites. Study on the risk management factors is scarce. The construction firms in Kerala lack a risk management framework and still practice the conventional construction process. The research for this study was conducted in private sector construction firms which provides access to the present conditions of the construction projects. Further, the research identifies the risks involved in handling construction projects, provides risk assessment based on the HIRA technique, and provides response strategies to critical risks. Thus, the study suggests various recommendations that can be utilized to reduce the impact of uncertainties on project performance, which is required because such high impact risks affects and slow down the performance of infrastructure projects.

articleTitle: Embedded Software Design in Orbital Module Sequencer for Manned Space Missions
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The reliability and fault-free operation of avionics systems in the crew module of manned space missions is of utmost importance. The orbital module sequencer (OMS) is a critical processor based system that executes sequencing commands. The MIL-STD-1553B bus serves as the communication medium between the crew module OBC and the OMS. The design and development of the real time, embedded software in OMS is covered in this work. The main functions of the OMS software are initializing the processor at power-on, handling transitions between modes, servicing telecommands, fault handling, data selection and synchronization. The steps followed in testing and validation of the software are also elaborated. The proper functioning of the software is ensured before clearing it for flight usage.

articleTitle: Classification of Emotions from Speech Signal Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Communication is essential for clearly expressing one's thoughts and ideas. Among all the different types of human communication, speech is the most preferred and powerful mode of expression. In terms of data, feature selection, and detection, this system outperforms an existing system. A methodology aiming at more precisely identifying speech percepts based on emotions. Recognition of emotion from speech signals is an essential but challenging task of Human-Computer Interaction. The task involves extracting the emotional content from the speech signals. It is quite challenging to extract emotion-oriented features from speech. In this case, we are using Mel Frequency Cepstral Coefficients to extract features. It is possible to classify natural emotions using various methods. In this paper we are recognized emotions using two different databases. One is RAVDESS database to extract emotions such as Neutral, Angry, Sad and happy and achieved recognition accuracy of 78.56%. Another one is Malayalam database created from different movie clips to extract emotions such as Neutral, Angry and Sad and achieved recognition accuracy of 84.3%. The aim of this paper is to classify models based on a MLP (multilayer perceptron) classifier. There are several intelligent services that consider the humanization of communication between humans and computers. Services such as chat-bots, cognitive diagnostics, medical intelligence, and marketing. As more and more people use mobile devices, the use of speech is becoming increasingly popular for interpersonal and human-to-machine communication. Among the applications are dialogue systems for spoken languages such as call center conversations and onboard vehicle driving systems that use emotion patterns in the speech.

articleTitle: Stability Enhancement of an Autonomous Microgrid using an Internal Model-based Controller
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The microgrid concept is gaining momentum to meet growing energy needs in autonomous mode. In autonomous mode, due to interaction through power electronics-based converter and low inertia of the DERs, microgrid stability is crucial. In literature, different control strategies are proposed with a passive load. The majority of which either vary the droop controller or droop constant parameters. However, the enhancement in microgrid transient response and stability is inadequate. The microgrids can be subjected to active, passive, or dynamic load. The active load consists of a rectifier whose dynamics are similar to those of an inverter control loop. Hence, the stability of an autonomous microgrid with active load is enhanced using voltage and current controllers based on an internal model-control approach (IMC) in this paper. The efficacy of an IMC-based controller is demonstrated through time-domain simulation and eigenvalue analysis, and the obtained results are compared with a traditional approach-based PI controller. The eigenvalue analysis and time-domain results show that IMC-based controllers significantly improve the transient response and damping of the critical modes.

articleTitle: Impact of Congestion and Demand Responsiveness on Market Power in Deregulated Power System
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: This paper presents the theoretical analysis of impact of congestion and demand responsiveness in mitigating market power of the GENCOs in the deregulated power system. For achieving the same, a new index naming Market Revenue Share (MRS) has been devised. Using this index, it has been analyzed that ability of generators to exercise market power will be reduced with the impact of demand responsiveness in imperfect electricity market. MRS index has been calculated as a percentage revenue share of the individual generator based on total market revenue earned by all the generators during any specific time span. The effectiveness of a proposed index has been demonstrated on IEEE-30 bus test system. Values of the market power and MRS Index are compared in both congested and uncongested transmission network. Results of this study, reflect that due to congestion, market power increases whereas it declines due to demand responsiveness. In other words, due to demand responsiveness, decrease in the value of MRS index of producers (having the ability to exercise market power) triggers reduction in market power of the particular generator in the deregulated electricity industry.

articleTitle: Economic Load Dispatch augmented with Environmental Considerations
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: In the past, researchers have paid a lot of attention to the Economic Dispatch of thermal units. There is a need to redefine the problem due to the high penetration of renewable resources. This research presents a combined emission economic dispatch for renewable integrated power system with six thermal units. Particle Swarm Optimization is a technique used for formulating and solving optimization problems with numerous constraints, such as power balance, generator bounds, reactive power limits, bus voltage bounds, solar power availability and solar penetration limits, valve point effect, environmental considerations, and line thermal capacity limits. It contributes in selecting the best combination of power to meet demand while minimising total cost of thermal units and successfully maximising renewable energy share, thereby lowering the thermal unit's environmental impact.

articleTitle: Classification of Paddy Diseases Using Ellipse Fitting
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Plant diseases are major threats to the agriculture sector which adversely affect the Indian economy. Correct identification of plant diseases is important for choosing preventive measures. Paddy is a widely consumed and cultivated food crop. Brown spot and leaf blast are two fungal diseases that affect paddy. There occurs a minor difference in the shape of the spots caused by these two diseases. Image processing techniques can be used to identify disease infected segments and calculate disease spread. The proposed system aims to classify brown spot and leaf blast diseases in paddy. It first segments the disease-affected region and calculates the disease spread in terms of area. Morphological operations enable the complete inclusion of the infected region by hole filling. The system is capable of detecting disease at a premature stage by detecting even mild infected spots. Then ellipse fitting is applied to the segmented images and the ratio of the length of the major axis to the minor axis is calculated. The ratio calculated for the two classes is used to define a threshold, which is used to classify the images. The system achieves 97% accuracy in classifying these two diseases.

articleTitle: Magneto-Static Analysis of a shower tray trap
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: This article presents study of magnet on shower tray trap. 3D model of the magnetic shower tray trap is designed and based on its dimensions a 2D model of magnets is created and magneto-static analysis is conducted. The main objective of this study is to compare the performance of various magnetic materials. The study of magneto static analysis is conducted and then force and torque induced by the interaction between iron based permanent magnets is calculated The geometric modelling of components are designed using SOLIDWORKS software. Then the model is imported to ANSYS Maxwell where the 2D analysis is conducted. Cost analysis is also conducted at the final stage to select the magnet for the trap.

articleTitle: Chest Abnormality Detection from X-Rays Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Coronavirus (COVID19) is a highly contagious virus which had already killed thousands of people and infected millions more throughout the world. One of the primary challenges that medical practitioners encounter in the realm of healthcare is correctly diagnosing patients conditions and infections. So far, the gold standard screening method RT-PCR test which has been designed to detect covid-19 which only has a positive rate ranging between 30 precent and 60 percent. As a result, a system that can accurately identify images and diagnose or anticipate diseases is needed. As a result, we set out to swiftly create a compact CNN architecture capable of recognizing COVID-19-infected individuals. Different CNN architectures are suggested in this paper to extract information from X-rays which further classified into Covid-19, pneumonia, or healthy. Here, we have used two datasets from publically available repositories that are Kaggle and Mendeley [1] [2]. To see how the size of datasets affects CNN performance, we train the suggested CNNs with both the original and enhanced datasets where datasets are splitted into ratios of 80:20 and 70:30 and the comparison is shown. Also suggested CNN model is compared with the five state-of-art pre-trained models (VGG-16, ResNet50, InceptionV3, EfficientNetB2, DenseNet121) with the same datasets and splitting ratios. we have also used Some visualization methods through which we can get an exact idea of how CNN functions and the explanation behind the network's decisions. This study suggests a model for classifying COVID-19 patients but makes no claims about medical diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Single Current Regulator Based Field Weakening Strategy For PMSM Drives and Experimental Validation using HIL
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors (PMSM) are widely used in traction purposes. It has the advantage of high efficiency, robustness, and good control characteristics. For the traction purpose, field weakening control is required to obtain wide speed operation. When the voltage reaches its maximum value, speed extension is possible by weakening the air gap flux. Direct weakening of air gap flux is not possible while it is possible by applying a demagnetising stator current. The conventional methods of flux weakening strategies are feed-forward flux weakening strategy and feed-back fluxweakening strategy. Feed-forward method depends upon the motor parameters an this leads to the instability of the system. The utilization of two current PI regulators leads to the saturation problems also. A Single Current Regulator (SCR) based flux weakening strategy is used to remove the saturation problem. In this strategy, dc bus voltage is fully utilized and provides better dynamic response. The simulation of the presented control is done by using MATLAB-Simulink and experimental evaluation is done using Typhoon HIL-402 in RBS mode.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of OFDM-IM Systems over Generalized $\kappa-\mu$ and $\eta-\mu$ Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: In this paper, average bit error rate (ABER) performance of an orthogonal frequency division multiplexing with index modulation (OFDM-IM) system, which is a strong transmission technology candidate for next-generation networks, has been analyzed over generalized fading models, namely eta-mu <tex>$(\eta-\mu)$</tex> and kappa-mu <tex>$(\kappa-\mu)$</tex> fading channels. These models have the advantage of simple algebraic notation, line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) propagation effects. The <tex>$\kappa-\mu$</tex> fading channel model is a LOS distribution, that includes the Nakagami-m and the Rice (Nakagami-n) distributions. Similarly, the special cases of <tex>$\eta-\mu$</tex> fading channel model are Hoyt, Rayleigh, Nakagami-m and One-sided Gaussian distributions. The effect of <tex>$\eta-\mu$</tex> and <tex>$\kappa-\mu$</tex> fading channel characteristics on the ABER performance of OFDM-1M systems was shown via computer simulations.

articleTitle: Bus Clamped PWM Based Vector Control of PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: This paper deals with the analysis of the vector controlled Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) drive operated with different types of space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) techniques. Different control techniques are available for the speed control of the PMSM drive. Vector control is the most significant control method. It gives better performance, since it is possible to control the flux and torque separately. Vector control is known as decoupled control or independent Control. The harmonic profile of the machine is affected by the type of Pulse width technique used. This paper evaluates the vector control strategy of PMSM drive based on conventional space vector pulse width modulation (CSVPWM) fed inverter and Bus clamped pulse width modulation (BCPWM) fed inverter.

articleTitle: Generation of Real-Time RF switching signal by polarization-dependent Four Wave Mixing technique
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The progress of the wireless frequency signal, including phase, frequency and amplitude, is the basic switching characteristics for the development of security of signal, the signal strength, and the rapid RF framework for upgrading the data capacity. It is not very difficult to convert the feasibility of the radio frequency signal to the GHz speed, though, it is very difficult to perform the phase or frequency exchange of radio frequency signals with rapid exchange time in the pico-seconds range. This article presents the current RF signal strategy and displayed in connection with the polarization of the four wave scheme that depends on a very non-linear optical fiber. The proposed system due to the amplitude, phase and frequency characteristics of FWM, is suitable for controlling multidimensional RF signals of GHz frequency, as well as the frequency and phase exchange of the GHz of the RF signal. Switching time is not only limited to the proposed switching scheme but also depends on the fluctuation or lifting/falling period of the control signal. In addition to the proposed RF signal switching method, not only the simultaneous frequency and phase exchange of gigahertz RF signals is implemented, but also the generation of a frequency signal with an exchange period of ps range. The 16-QAM signal is modulated at a frequency of 10 GHz and the spectrum is analyzed. The electrical constellation of 16-QAM is viewed and the eye diagram is simulated with this proposed system. The simulation is analyzed and demonstrated in Optisystem software.

articleTitle: Nonlinearity Mitigation in Radio over Fiber Network using Nonlinear Fourier Transform based Optical Fiber link
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Radio over Fiber (RoF) is a wireless network technology which combines Radio Frequency (RF) link with Optical Fiber (OF) Link so as to improve the channel capacity. Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) based RoF (OFDM-RoF) is an advancement in RoF utilizing the merits of OFDM, which is a multi-carrier modulation scheme that efficiently reduces Inter-Symbol-Interference (ISI) and offers high data rate. Since optical fiber link is a major part of RoF network, fiber-nonlinearity acts as an impairment to the network. Thus our design objective is to find a solution to the nonlinear limits in RoF system. In this paper, we propose a system model for nonlinearity compensation in RoF network, that utilizes a class of Nonlinear Fourier Transform (NFT) based OF link known as the Nonlinear Frequency Division Multiplexing (NFDM), which is a nonlinear analogy of OFDM.

articleTitle: Impact of Boron doping in spin coated ZnO Thin Film Transistors
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Transparent conductive oxides are developed as a possible replacement for the traditional silicon and organic semiconductors within the field of microelectronics. Transparency property, good carrier mobility and enormous area uniformity makes them appropriate for the applications like transparent light emitting diodes, liquid displays, sensors and X-ray detectors. The optical transparency property in solution processed thin films have opened a replacement horizon for low-cost transparent electronic circuits and devices. Here we report the event of a high performance and operationally stable metal oxide semiconductor thin film Transistors. By sol-gel spin coating method Zinc Oxide doped with Boron is used as the channel layer of the thin film transistor. Structural and optical studies are analyzed to understand the performance of doped Zinc Oxide layer. The electrical properties were also measured using a semiconductor parameter analyzer.

articleTitle: Effect of PZT patch length on Piezo electric Energy Harvester
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: All structures in nature have vibration energy which can be converted into Electrical energy. This electrical energy can be used as a source of energy to operate sensors thereby replacing limited storage capacity equipment's such as battery. Piezoelectric vibration energy harvesting scheme utilizes direct piezoelectric effect to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy. The output voltage from the piezoelectric vibration energy harvester depends on the relative motion between the base and proof mass. The resulted mechanical strain developed on the PZT patches is converted into electrical power because of direct coupling piezo electric effect. This article present a study of the effect of length of PZT patch on single modal linear vibration based piezo electric energy harvester (PEH). A coupled series piezo patch-electrical circuit finite element model is used to analyze the power output of a vibration based piezoelectric energy-harvesting device (EHD) when it is connected to a load resistor. Mathematical model of linear single modal Vibration -based Energy harvester is developed using Ansys APDL (Ansys parametric design Language). The modeling configuration is done with a series configuration of piezo electric layers. Accuracy of the developed FEM model is validated against the existing coupled FEM model. First modal analysis is performed to find the natural frequency of the piezoelectric energy harvester. Then harmonic analysis is carried out to estimate the voltage responses and power output which are measured through the PZT patches.

articleTitle: Structural Health Monitoring aided by neural networks
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Despite of the age of the building and the nature of materials used in it, it is important to retain the reliability and service life of structures. This is established by proper monitoring of various structural members. A distress may occur in a structure due to numerous reasons from shrinkage cracks due to hot weather at the time of concreting to chloride induced corrosion or creep deflections at later stages. Due to the diversity in the factors that cause structural distress, proper recognition becomes quintessential. The R&D in the field of structural design is progressing day by day. So is the amendments in the codal provisions related to it. This paper intends to contemplate the available latest structural health monitoring mechanisms based on pertinent literature. The main emphasis of the paper is on the need for proper monitoring of existing and upcoming structures and also to employ proper monitoring techniques. The limitations in existing knowledge and lack of codal provisions can be tackled by suitable monitoring techniques. For forthcoming constructions, monitoring mechanisms could be used for validating design assumptions and software analysis results. These could be achieved by proper incorporation of building information modelling (BIM), sensors and neural networks. There have been serious structural failures, which could have been avoided by providing necessary retrofitting based on inspection. This flaw of not inspecting and monitoring of constructed structures could be tackled by structural health monitoring techniques and this could be made convenient by use of neural networks. Thus, making structural maintenance economical, as remedy is started at initial stage itself.

articleTitle: Integrated Control and Monitoring Systems in Urban Sewage Treatment Plants Using Advanced Process system
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The continuous improvement of the manufacturing sector and the quick development of metropolitan areas, a substantial amount of manufacturing and household sewage is discharged untreated into water resources. The increasing shortage of water resources means efficient and reliable sewage treatment has become an important link in realizing sustainable development, and the intelligent upgrading of sewage monitoring systems has become essential in the control of sewage treatment. The standardization of computerization control for urban sewage treatment plants, such as industrial waste and home waste, is a major challenge. Sewage treatment plants that use activated sludge treatment are frequently used to purify sewage water. The Siemens PCS7 control platform is produced by the primary research object and is a fundamental monitoring tool for detecting the PH and COD levels in treated sewage. The S7-400 series controller applies the closed loop PID control system and the model predictive control system. An enhanced sewage monitoring impact has been obtained with the appropriate development of PCS structure and Profinet network level in sewage treatment systems with Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition as the platform. Systems management for process automation pushed techniques that allowed access to field device, controller, and SCADA system operations and data. Optimize the functioning of a sewage treatment facility in terms of process stability, energy consumption, and environmental compliance.

articleTitle: Internet of Things Security and Forensics: Concern and Challenges for Inspecting Cyber Attacks
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The Internet of Things is an emerging technology for recent marketplace. In IoT, the heterogeneous devices are connected through the medium of the Internet for seamless communication. The devices used in IoT are resource-constrained in terms of memory, power and processing. Due to that, IoT system is unable to implement hi-end security for malicious cyber-attacks. The recent era is all about connecting IoT devices in various domains like medical, agriculture, transport, power, manufacturing, supply chain, education, etc. and thus need to be prevented from attacks and analyzed after attacks for legal action. The legal analysis of IoT data, devices and communication is called IoT forensics which is highly indispensable for various types of attacks on IoT system. This paper will review types of IoT attacks and its preventive measures in cyber security. It will also help in ascertaining IoT forensics and its challenges in detail. This paper will conclude with the high requirement of cyber security in IoT domains with implementation of standard rules for IoT forensics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Student's Learning Perception of Online Classes in Polytechnic colleges and Engineering programmes in Kerala
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Educational institutions and students find it a challenging task to complete the syllabus prescribed in the given period of academic year in compliance with the academic calendar, as they remain closed for an indefinite period due to the outbreak of Covid. Efforts are being made by them to chalk out ways n means to achieve the goal of completing the portions of syllabus well in time in spite of the hostile situation. Assurance of quality of learning is also a matter of prime importance for which the content has to be designed well and delivered in a professional manner. Most of the students face constraints in learning through online platform and as such it deserves high attention as to how the content is organized and presented before them so as to address such constraints and to make the learning effective. As the pandemic and subsequent restrictions led to the sudden change from conventional class room to online mode, teachers and students have faced much challenges. Most of the institutions couldn't rise to the occasion so as to formulate quality contents to deliver through online platform. Online learning can be made easy, efficient and productive if the experiences of students and learning are incorporated in the study. The findings of this study indicated that majority of the students evinced a positive attitude towards online classes in the wake of corona. The online learning was found to be advantageous as it provided flexibility and convenience for the learners. Students preferred well-structured content with recorded videos uploaded in university web-sites. They also indicated the need for interactive sessions with quizzes and assignments at the end of each class to optimize the learning experience.

articleTitle: Automated Hyperparameter Optimization in Machine Learning for Stock Prediction
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Stock prediction is the key area of focus in financial analysis. The growing amount of data and readily available machine learning algorithms has surged the amount of research in this field. This research in particular, involved in stock prediction of NEPSE using machine learning algorithms such as Linear Regression and LSTM. The research also studied traditional financial models such as ARIMA and GARCH. The analysis involved in manual and automated hyperparameter optimization via Optuna framework for single and stacked LSTM models. Initially, traditional financial models performed better than manually optimized LSTM variants. But the automated hyperparameter tuning approach significantly lowered the error loss and the single LSTM model best predicted the stock price with 7.21 RMSE score. https://github.com/SudipBishwakarma/MSc-Dissertation-2021.

articleTitle: Survey paper on the Forward Kinematics Solution of a Stewart Platform
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Over the past few decades, researchers have become increasingly interested in the Stewart Platform, a parallel manipulator with six degrees of freedom (DOF) that offers remarkable functionality over serial manipulators. The main objection to the implementation of closed loop control in Stewart Platform is its difficulty in solving the forward kinematics. In the forward kinematics problem, the pose and orientation of the moving platform are determined from the leg lengths. This is a high degree nonlinear problem with multiple solutions. Even though many studies were conducted about the kinematics of parallel robots, forward kinematics continues to be a hindrance to its practical application. Consequently, the real-time solution of forward kinematics is gaining interest. To address the direct kinematics problem, several approaches were presented, including numerical techniques, analytical methods, sensor-based methods, methods using neural networks, and observer-based methods. In this paper, the different approaches and limitations of the forward kinematics problem on Stewart Platform are analyzed.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Approach for Breast Cancer Detection using Thermal Imaging
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Breast cancer is the worldwide major cause of death in women. With the advancement of techniques for breast cancer diagnosis, certain risk factor is also there with exposure to radiation. Thermal imaging of breast for cancer diagnosis receive interest in various literatures that detect the thermal activity in the precancerous tissues and surrounding areas. Patients with malignant breast tumour have a greater rate of survival if they are caught early. It has been found that analyzing the textural and color feature of breast thermograms aids in offering more accurate information for diagnosis. Breast thermograms from 200 individuals (100 healthy and 100 sick) from the Database Mastology Research (DMR) visual laboratories were used in this study. In particular, the Gray level co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture features are retrieved using five commonly used descriptors: energy, correlation, homogeneity, entropy, and contrast. RGB, HSV, and LAB color spaces are used to extract color features. The objective of this paper is to utilize various machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, linear discriminant analysis and k-nearest neighbor using textural and color features for the classification of breast cancer on thermal images. The KNN classifier perform best among other classifiers, hence may provide support to healthcare industries in the development of computer aided preliminary screening of cancerous images.

articleTitle: Using BIM for Residential Projects in Kerala-Challenges and Possibilities
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: The overall aim of this paper is to analyze the possibilities of applying Building Information Modelling in designing and building of houses with special reference to Kerala, India. The paper starts with a brief study to understand BIM as a tool in building detailing and construction. It is followed by a literature study to understand the benefits of using BIM in small scale residences. Literature case studies from around the world show successful examples of houses detailed out and constructed using BIM, in small scale and integrating vernacular details. Online surveys to understand the possible challenges and potentials for implementing it in design and construction of houses in Kerala are done through social media among designers and the results are discussed. The paper concludes by proposing a possible method for overcoming the challenges and encouraging the implementation of Building Information Modelling for detailing and building of houses in Kerala by integrating vernacular details in the tool. The paper also recommends popularizing the usage of BIM in Kerala through a campaigning on social media.

articleTitle: Sustainability in Architectural Education in India
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: India is the second most populated country in the world with more than one-sixth of the world's population. The construction sector in India contributes to global warming, poor air quality and other such sustainability related concerns. Architectural education in India should take a holistic and sustainable approach to mitigate the challenges and issues fueled by unchecked urbanization. This paper focuses on the thrust given to the education of sustainability concerns in architecture. The first part is a qualitative and exploratory study of the syllabi and curricula of 15 institutions who impart architectural education in India. Institutions within the first 15 ranks in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) ranking 2021 have been chosen for the comparative study. The later part consists of survey questionnaires aimed to assess the degree of inclusion of sustainability concerns in architectural curriculum from educators' and students' perspective. A total of 114 responses from educators and 200 responses from students were received from varied institutions across India. It is found that curriculum review is required to integrate sustainability in architectural education in India.

articleTitle: Indigenous Knowledge system of Kerala Fisherfolks to mitigate coastal hazard: A Case of Thiruvananthapuram District
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Coastal hazards are often unpredictable but if we are able to understand the indigenous knowledge system that is prevalent among the fisherfolk, then suitable mitigation measures could be adopted for disaster risk reduction. The study explores the role of indigenous knowledge system in fishing activities as well as prediction of coastal hazards in fishing village of Vizhinjam in Thiruvananthapuram district of Kerala state. A lot of development projects are going on in the capital city of Kerala state. Due to lack of proper planning and community participation many of such development projects cause adverse environmental impacts that lead to increase in vulnerability to hazards. Key informant interview, focus group discussion and researcher observation were used to collect data for the study. Snow balling technique was used to identify key informants. One of the major findings was that the fisherfolk has the capacity to identify and respond to hazardous situation quickly due to the indigenous practices they possess. This paper concludes with a suggestion that application and integration of indigenous knowledge system with the scientific realm helps to develop accurate forecast and warning measures which thereby would facilitate effective mitigation of hazards in coastal area.

articleTitle: Advancements in Failure Mode and Effect Analysis: A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Failure modes and effect analysis (FMEA) is a risk prioritization technique mainly used by manufacturing and process industries. In FMEA, the impact of a particular failure mode is calculated using three risk factors. These are severity (S), occurrence (O), and detection (D). This method is suitable for failure determination in processes, designs, products, software, supply chains, etc. This paper includes a systematic review of the advancements in conventional FMEA. Initially, the drawbacks of traditional FMEA are listed to show the scope for improvement. Then the concept of assigning weight to each factor using the analytic hierarchy process (AHP) is studied. The AHP-FMEA with other risk factors is provided in the next part. The second session of this paper contains an overview of seven types of FMEA integration. They are failure mode and effect anticipatory analysis (FMEAA), fuzzy FMEA, FMEA using fuzzy logic and grey relation theory (GRT), hybrid multilevel fault tree analysis (FTA)-FMEA method, FMEA based on Dempster-Shafer Theory (DST), geometric mean FMEA based on information quality, and ambiguity measure weighted risk priority number (AMWRPN) model.

articleTitle: Self-Attention Architecture for Ingredients Generation from Food Images
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Food filming is becoming more popular among food connoisseurs. Each meal has a narrative that is detailed in a lengthy recipe, and sadly, just looking at a dish provides no insight into the preparation of food. There are various websites that aid in recognizing a meal by its components; however, no method has been successful at forecasting the ingredients in a dish. As a consequence, this research proposes a method for automatically generating the dish's recipe. This approach estimates the image's title and ingredients and then generates the image's featured meal's specific cooking instructions. This investigation looked at a range of Indian cuisines, including lunch and breakfast. To enhance user-friendly, this paper provides a web application that displays the recipe with a photograph of the dish.

articleTitle: IMPROVING SENSITIVITY OF ZnO NANORODS FOR THE APPLICATION OF GAS SENSORS AT LOW TEMPERATURES: A REVIEW
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is a nontoxic, affordable, plentiful, and chemically stable substance. Harmful and low concentration gases are detected by using ZnO nanorods because of range of conductance, response towards of oxidative, sensitive and selective properties.This paper review on various fabrication process of ZnO nanorods and their modifications for improving sensitivity for gas sensors at low temperatures. Fabrication methods of Zinc Oxide Nanorods comprise of hydrothermal method, microemulsion, microwave-assisted hydrolysis preparation, gas-solution-solid method and so on. ZnO Nanorods during the fabrication can be controlled by selective growth, control growth and regulating its diameter. Zinc Oxide Nanorods can be modified by doping, surface functionalization and sensitizing the sensing layer with metals and metal oxides.Due to ZnO's limited operation at low temperatures, the majority of research is focused on detecting gases at high working temperatures (200-500C), which would inevitably increase energy consumption and reduce sensor lifespan. Finally, the problems and potential development directions of ZnO-based gas sensors at low temperatures are discussed.

articleTitle: An Abridged Review of Transfer Learning Technology
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Computer vision studies have adapted several deep learning approaches to achieve desired results. One of such approaches is transfer learning, which uses pre-trained models as a starting point for computer vision tasks. A model is trained with particular dataset to recognize certain patterns. There are lots of models namely ResNet, VGG-16, MobileNet, Inception etc. These models are trained on more than a million images from the ImageNet database. By using transfer learning technology a model can be reused in a new problem. Typically, in computer vision, neural networks try to detect edges in the first layer, shapes in the intermediate layer, and task-specific properties in the latter layers. Transfer learning uses the early and central layers, while the subsequent layers are only retrained. Transfer learning performs several beneficial functions, including reducing training time, improving neural network performance, and reducing dataset size. Transfer learning has become a promising and popular deep learning field because of its extensive application possibilities. This survey analyses the existing transfer learning research studies, which can help upcoming researchers to better understand current research level and concepts in transfer learning. A review of 20 transfer learning approaches is presented in this survey.

articleTitle: Computer Assisted Recognition of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Using GLCM Features in Haar Wavelet Transformed Space and Random Forest Classifier
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Oral cancer is a dangerous disease which is mainly seen among men compared to women across the world. Oral cancer can cause death if it is not diagnosed early. Among the oral cancer types, oral squamous cell carcinoma is commonly seen. Detection of oral cancer is done using the histopathology images. Since histopathology images have different tissue and nucleus structures, feature extraction is always difficult. We propose a method for feature extraction and classification of oral histopathology images into normal or cancerous (Oral squamous cell carcinoma). In the proposed method, the normal and oral squamous cell carcinoma histopathology images are decomposed into one approximation and three detail coefficients by Haar wavelets. Features are then extracted from the high frequency and low-frequency coefficients with the Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix. The features are fused to obtain a feature vector and the relevant features are selected by using an extra trees classifier. Finally, we used Random forest, K Nearest Neighbour and Voting classifier for the binary classification into normal and cancerous. The performance of the algorithm is evaluated using the performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, confusion matrix, sensitivity, specificity, F1 score, Quality index, error rate, ROC curves and AUC values of characteristic curves. Among the classifiers, Random forest gives high accuracy of 97.59% and a precision of 95.98%. The proposed method for detecting oral cancer is effective and precise. Hence, it can be used as a reliable and accurate support tool for oral pathologists.

articleTitle: A Review on Aspect Based Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Sentiment analysis, otherwise called emotion AI, is the computational analysis of raw data that uses text to detect a person's sentiment. Opinions and feelings are communicated more frequently and extensively than ever before in the age of social media. The number of likes for social media opinions reveals which subjects are receiving the most attention, allowing companies and artists to better understand what their customers think of their products. As a result, the problem of picture or text sentiment categorization is of tremendous interest. Document level, phrase level, and aspect level sentiment analysis are the three ways for doing sentiment analysis. There are three major jobs at the aspect level. The most important and first objective is to recognise and extract question parts. The second goal is to identify the extremes of diverse points of view on various characteristics: positive, negative, and neutral. Next task is determined by compiling a list of terms that are similar to features. The goal of aspect-level sentiment analysis is to predict the sentiment polarity of each individual aspect term in a sentence, which is a notable challenge in natural language processing. Fine-grained sentiment analysis at the aspect level is a research hotspot.

articleTitle: An Entropy based approach to investigate the heterogeneous sensory pattern in Autism Spectrum Disorders
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: Sensory hyper-or hypo-responsivity, which imparts heterogeneity to Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD), adversely affects the communication skills, classroom learning and independent living of such individuals. The need of the hour is to provide targeted medical intervention to the neurobiologically distinct subgroups present in ASD. Hence, the proposed work is aimed at examining the heterogeneity and identifying the hyper-responsive subgroup in ASD. The current study employs entropy-based measure calculated over multiple time scales to study the complexity pattern of the Visual Evoked Potential (VEP) signals recorded from a group of 30 subjects, diagnosed with ASD. The VEP signals are measured in response to visual stimuli consisting of vertical achromatic sinewave gratings presented under low (5%), medium (50%) and high (90%) contrasts. After pre-processing, the VEP signals are decomposed into 5 modes using Variational Mode Extraction as follows: mode 1 (0–4 Hz), mode 2 (4–8 Hz), mode 3 (8–16 Hz), mode 4 (16–32 Hz) and mode 5 (32–64 Hz). Improved Multiscale Permutation Entropy (IMPE) is extracted from these modes and Relative Complexity (RC) analysis is carried out across varying contrasts. The IMPE-based RC analysis exhibits an increasing complexity pattern which is an indication of hyper-responsivity and is further statistically verified through Friedman test. This pattern is observed in 43% of the ASD study population in modes 2 and 3, which correspond to theta and alpha bands of brain signal frequencies.

articleTitle: Analysis of Driver Behaviour Towards Road Safety Measures Using Driver Behaviour Questionnaire
publicationTitle: 2022 Second International Conference on Next Generation Intelligent Systems (ICNGIS)
abstract: A common instrument for assessing unusual driving behaviour is the Driver Behaviour Questionnaire (DBQ). Despite the prominence of the self-report approach, DBQ implementation in developing countries like India has gone unnoticed. The purpose of this study is to use the DBQ to examine abnormal driving behaviour toward road safety measures and to look into the association between demographic characteristics and abnormal driver behaviour and traffic offences. According to exploratory factor analysis (EFA) on surveyed data, the derived three-factor, namely offence, fault, and lapse, categorises the degree of aberrant driving behaviours. Additionally, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), which is also a strong fit for behaviour prediction, was used to verify the model's validity and reliability. Important data on the effects of demographics on driving behaviour were found, and this information will help preventative measures be developed in the future.
